cells.tense: What you're tending is growing under your hands right now, and you're steady at it.
cells.ask: offer one small thing you've been holding back to the people who benefit from it, and let them say thank you.
cells.core:
You know how to hold weight without clamping down, and how to let things grow without overwatering them. Standing in a room where two people need opposite things, you keep both of them alive instead of picking a favorite — and you do it without ceremony, so nobody notices it took anything out of you. That's the shape of the care: quiet, steady, still going.

The steady hold carries a lot without asking for anything back. Hand one piece of it into the open this week. Let it be seen and named, even briefly — not for applause, so the effort stops living only inside you.
cells.sheetLine: What you tend is growing, and the holding is steady.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: the place that holds weight without breaking

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a load nobody has handed you yet, and the steady hold has gone tight.
cells.ask: replay one thing that already worked out and let that be enough before you plan the next fix.
cells.core:
When the holding is working, it sits down with what's already finished and lets it be finished. There's a weight it knows to put down, and it puts it down without a speech. The garden gets tended and then left alone to grow, and that's enough for the day.

The holding is strong, but right now it's running ahead of what exists. You're gripping a future that can't be written in, checking on it before it's real, planning the next repair before the current thing has had a chance to settle. That's not care anymore; it's grip. The weight you're carrying is one you made up in advance. Do the finishing with one thing today, and let the steady part come back — the energy that's stuck can turn from guarding into something that actually satisfies.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a harvest that hasn't grown yet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: the place that holds weight without breaking

cells.tense: The holding effort stopped a while back, and you're still standing at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.ask: pick one thing you still want and hope for it out loud, once, to yourself or someone safe.
cells.core:
When the hold is working, there's something you're carrying toward and the carrying has an end in sight. You get up for it, keep at it through the long middle, and it matters that you kept at it. That's what the strength is for.

Right now nothing is being tended. Supplies ran low and the holding stopped — not because the load was too heavy, but because the fuel for carrying it got spent. What's missing isn't strength. It's the wanting that makes strength possible. What's still alive in you is the wanting. Water that, not the discipline. Hope for something small, and keep hoping for it even after it doesn't arrive on time. That's what pulls the hold back into your hands.
cells.sheetLine: The hold went empty and stayed empty.

cells.tense: You're carrying it daily — the tending, the weighing of what's needed — but you talk as if it were doing itself.
cells.ask: say out loud that one thing you keep maintaining is something you chose, and let someone hear you call it yours.
cells.core:
When someone tends something well, they can name what they're holding and why it's theirs to hold. The care has a hand on it — a person behind it, choosing it, saying so without fuss.

You're already tending something, and tending it well, but you'd describe it as just handling things. The care is steady enough that it looks automatic to you. It isn't automatic. You stood up for it, kept it alive, and made the calls that held it together. That's the part nobody sees, including you. Let one piece of it be witnessed. Name what you chose and what it cost. The hold isn't complete until the one doing the holding gets to stop pretending it was nothing.
